models_evaluated: Llama 3.2 with RAG (Sentence-BERT, FAISS, cross-encoder re-ranking)

links.outcome: Hallucination rate, faithfulness and factual accuracy with vs without retrieval grounding
links.effect: RAG reduced hallucination rate from 47.8% to 12.3% (74.3% relative reduction); Faithfulness 0.52 to 0.87; Factual Accuracy 0.54 to 0.89.
links.quote: Evaluated on a purpose-built dataset of 150 drug-related question–answer pairs spanning ten commonly used medications and multiple information categories, our RAG system reduces the hallucination rate from 47.8% to 12.3% — a 74.3% relative reduction — while improving Faithfulness from 0.52 to 0.87 and Factual Accuracy from 0.54 to 0.89.

screen.reason: Empirically evaluates the effect of adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounding to an LLM on drug-related question answering hallucination rates and factual accuracy.
